messages:
sarah: FYI ACME support case — several engineers report they can view projects but get "You don't have permission to perform this action" when clicking Edit / Manage settings. Happens in the console and via API (403). Started after last night's Okta group rename + SCIM sync.

sarah: Repro steps I ran:
```bash
# returns 403
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/projects/0xACME/edit \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-live-REDACTED" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"name":"acme-new"}'
```

sarah: API response body:
```json
{"error":"rbac.action_denied","message":"user not authorized to update project"}
```

alex: thanks, adding to this thread. can you paste the org id + one affected user id? also, do affected users show Project Admin in the console UI under Memberships?

sarah: org: 0xACMEORG, one example user: u_0xdev123. In console the role column shows "Project Admin" for them, but the action buttons are greyed and calls 403.

alex: sounds like a role-binding mismatch (group mapping). quick check: can you run the admin rolebindings endpoint and paste the entry for this project?

sarah: ran: `GET /v1/admin/rolebindings?org=0xACMEORG&project=0xACME` -> got back group mapping pointing to `okta:acme-devs ` (note trailing space). suspect SCIM trimmed/normalized during the rename.

alex: that trailing whitespace would definitely break group equality when auth checks are done. SCIM/Okta sometimes strips whitespace on rename. two short fixes: 1) force a SCIM resync to re-evaluate group membership->role bindings, or 2) temporary manual fix: create a rolebinding alias matching the trimmed name.

alex: to force resync (ops perms required):
```bash
# schedule immediate SCIM group resync for the org
redwood-admin scim resync --org 0xACMEORG --groups --force
```

infra-bot: SCIM resync job queued (job id: job_889223). will run in ~10s.

mike: from product side - if this is SCIM normalization, we should also add a short heuristic in the binding matcher to trim whitespace to avoid customer-visible breakage. filing follow-up.

ops: while job runs, as a short-term workaround we can re-invite affected users or reapply the rolebinding with the exact trimmed string. re-invite worked for 1 user earlier?

sarah: re-invite fixed 1/6 users. after resync job: 4/6 fixed automatically. 2 remain blocked. calling out that their auth tokens are likely cached.

alex: for the two remaining, can you ask them to sign out and sign back in (or revoke sessions)? we also have an admin command to flush cached auth entries: `redwood-admin cache flush --org 0xACMEORG --user u_0xdev123`.

sarah: ran cache flush + they re-signed. both regained edit access. marking customer case as mitigated.

mike: creating a product ticket to add defensive trimming and an alert when rolebindings reference group names with suspicious whitespace.

incident-bot: Ticket #CASE-2026 created and linked to this thread. severity: low-medium.

sarah: thanks all :thumbsup: will follow up with ACME CS to close the loop and share mitigation steps + ask Okta to avoid leading/trailing whitespace during group renames.
